name: Jersey Club
summary: Newark's bouncy descendant of Baltimore club, defined by the 5-kick skeleton — attacks on 16th positions 1, 5, 9, 12, 15 (gaps of 4-4-3-3-2) — that compresses into a tresillo-like 3-3-2 bounce over its back half. Sparse hats, chopped vocal stabs and a sampled 'bed squeak' fill the gaps; velocity variation rather than heavy swing carries the loose, never-quantized feel.

sounds.kick: Short, punchy kick (often doubled with an 808) run in the 5-hit skeleton; the last hit is the softest, shortest — a pickup rather than an accent.
sounds.snare: Clap sits against the kick run rather than a flat backbeat; Baltimore-lineage grooves use a real snare on 2 and 4 instead.
sounds.hats: Sparse — often just closed hat on 2 and 4; Philly-scene and 2020s drill-hybrid variants run denser 16th or triplet-feel hat rolls.
sounds.percussion: The sampled 'bed squeak' (from Trillville's 'Some Cut') and chopped vocal stabs mapped onto rim/perc roles are the genre's real percussive identity, not congas or shakers.
sounds.cymbals: Open hat used as a rhythmic 'skip' accent on the & of 2 and 4, not a cymbal wash; crash essentially unused.

machines: Roland TR-909 / TR-808 — kick and clap foundation for the 5-kick pattern
Akai MPC2000 / MPC3000 — chopping the Trillville 'bed squeak' and vocal hooks into stutter runs
E-mu SP-1200 — lo-fi resampling for grittier Baltimore-lineage breakbeat voicings
Elektron Machinedrum — synthesised hats and percussion for denser 2020s club/drill hybrids
Vocal chop sample packs (Jersey/Baltimore club specific) — the genre's actual hook material
references: DJ Tameil / Brick Bandits — Brick City club foundations
DJ Sliink — Jersey club international breakthrough
Cookiee Kawaii — Vibe (If I Back It Up) (2020)
